correctness.rationale: Unit-edge vertices, facet areas and normals are reconstructed. Cauchy’s formula gives an exact two-chamber area. Both chambers have explicit positive-ray decompositions proving the global minimum and unique symmetry orbit; Cauchy–Schwarz proves the sharp maximum and its unique symmetry orbit. Gaussian polar integration establishes the absolute-product kernel used to calculate the exact second moment. Seven embedded executable checks reconstruct face/edge counts, direct convex-hull areas, pair multiplicities and spherical integration corroboration. Exact claims need no finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: A three-dimensional regular truncated octahedron is a canonical space-filling Voronoi cell. Its random planar projection area is a natural measurement in imaging and integral geometry. The two-chamber brightness formula and sharp nonaxial maximum/minimum directions provide structural classification, and the exact second moment/variance calibrate orientation fluctuations beyond known mean-area identities; the particular shape and observable are not arbitrary numerical slicing.
